verdicts.note: Attacked on magnitude (could be -2) and on her lack of county office. S1 and S3 give 11 years as an elected school board director and 7 as superintendent, plus Ferry Advisory Committee chair since 2018; S8 has her calling herself 'the longest track record and ... most experienced, seasoned candidate'. She is not an incumbent, so -1 rather than -2 holds; high confidence is earned by her own explicit framing [S8]. Summary and highlights check out against S1, S3, S4, S5 and S9 (2,944 primary votes).

S5 ('This is not the time to expand county services ... live within our means'), S4 (efficiency, rebuild emergency reserves) and S1 (address the shortfall, rebuild reserves) support restraint. The counter-evidence, her list of priorities to protect (mandated services, seniors, parks, conservation) [S5], is triage within restraint, not expansion, so -1 rather than 0 holds. Not -2: she protects 'essential public services' [S4].

Checked whether the 0 is an 'unknown' 0. It is not: S5 holds explicit statements in both directions, reading the levy defeat as 'residents are not looking to pay more in property taxes' while promising 'alternative ways the county can increase revenue' for 2028. Her pledge to live within means [S4][S5] could argue -1, but she never opposes new revenue, so genuinely mixed at medium confidence stands. Highlight 3 accurately says she names no tax [S5].

Inconsistent with Bryant Ingman's 0. The basis itself lists code revisions to ease affordable development [S5], a pole_a supply tool and the same kind of evidence that made Bryant Ingman a 0. Her pole_b evidence is weaker than Bryant Ingman's: the land trust and teacher-housing fundraising [S3] are private nonprofit efforts, not public investment or tenant protection, and 'expand access to affordable housing for the full income diversity' [S4] names no mechanism, whereas Bryant Ingman commits to protecting and funding the public Home Fund. The contest file agrees the two differ in emphasis, not direction. Swanson's evidence is mixed: score 0. The highlight about the land trust and 'full income diversity' is accurate [S3][S4].

S4 ('Protecting our environment is of the utmost importance as we continue to see impacts to our islands from climate change') and S6 (took part in the April 2, 2026 Climate Convergence) support +1. Nothing in the dossier puts energy affordability first. Not +2: she proposes no specific climate program.

S9 ('With age doesn't always come more experience - sometimes we need to shake things up') and S1 (no elected experience) support +1 at high confidence; her generational pitch is explicit. Not +2: she also leans on a decade of nonprofit leadership [S1][S7]. Highlights check out: the Lopez Clinic transition is attributed in S5, S7 and S9 to the Catherine Washburn Medical Association she presides over; 'Led' follows her own framing ('which she says'), acceptable for a highlight.

Attacked toward 0: she would review management and administrative costs first, set per-program criteria and backs 'balanced budgets' [S1][S4][S5], all pole_a elements. But the thrust of S5 is to protect frontline services 'before cutting deeper', invest in deferred maintenance now ('Deferred maintenance always costs more later') and 'keep investing in affordable housing', with new revenue to pay for it. That leans pole_b; +1 at medium confidence is right, not higher.

S5 names new revenue tools (updated lodging taxes, short-term rental permitting, an added 0.1% law-and-justice sales tax, voluntary visitor taxes) and S9 records her disappointment that the levy lid lift failed, a cap lift the rubric places at pole_b. Her 'without asking islanders to shoulder more' [S5] and the tools' visitor-facing incidence keep it at +1, not +2. Highlight 3 matches S5.

S4 lists pole_a supply tools (ADU reforms, pre-approved plans, permit streamlining, a land-use capacity review); S5 commits to protecting and funding the county Home Fund (pole_b public investment). A genuine mix, not an unknown; 0 at medium stands. See the Swanson housing verdict for the consistency fix.
S4 (integrate the county Climate Action Plan across departments; resilience against climate-related challenges) and S6 (greater EV use) support +1. No cost-tradeoff statement either way; not +2.
